analysis.title: Global Rates Trader: Moving Deliberately
key_insights: GS sees risk-asset volatility as the main driver of global duration. The shift from energy risks to AI worries as the primary rates factor has re-coupled longer-term US forwards with fair value, but GS estimates real money is still underweight duration, leaving room for the rally to extend if risk volatility persists.

GS closes its receive 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly and adds a long 5s on the 2s5s30s UST fly. The reasons are reduced very front-end hike risk, 5s tending to outperform during and right after hiking cycles, and the long-end risk skew at next week's refunding.

The FOMC statement and Chair Warsh's press conference reinforced GS economists' every-other-meeting hike approach. The baseline is one more hike in December, with a risk of a third hike in March if inflation surprises up.

Warsh announced the Fed will devote one meeting next year and two in 2028 to broad policy strategy. The curve steepened on the news, which GS reads as a dovish interpretation of the schedule change. GS would be surprised if it constrained the Fed's ability to act when the case is clear.

The initial rates impact of next week's midterm elections likely depends on perceived implications for AI and on developments in the Iran conflict. If the weak risk tone persists, GS thinks the market is prone to react more strongly to a downside surprise in next Friday's labor market report.

GS expects Treasury at the refunding to keep 10-to-30y coupon auction sizes steady and hold or modestly raise buyback sizes. A cut in long-end sizes is a risk but not the base case. GS expects Treasury to signal future size adjustments and to begin raising 2-to-7y auction sizes in May 2027.

GS fair value models show long-end spreads still wide to fair value and the spread curve somewhat steep, while longer-term forwards are only modestly above fair value. Pressure has been at the very front end, where T-bills have cheapened versus OIS since late August on elevated bill supply, money funds shortening maturity and zero money fund AUM growth since summer.

GS thinks market expectations lean toward reduced long-end auction sizes, so unchanged sizes could disappoint and cause long-end underperformance on the spread curve. GS expects the impact to be contained.

The BoC raised rates 25bp as expected with a more hawkish tone but said policy will 'proceed carefully'. Markets price 13bp of hikes by year-end and about 100bp through end-2027. GS sees this front-end hike premium as excessive and favors CAD front-end flatteners.

GS gives three reasons the CAD front end is overpriced. Trim and median inflation are below 2%, and GS economists expect year-end 2027 inflation 40bp below the BoC's estimate. AI-trade volatility has weighed on peers' hike expectations. Upside data would more likely pull hikes forward than raise the cumulative amount priced.

The ECB is on track for a December hike. Lagarde's press conference pointed to a high bar not to hike, and GS expects the market to decay toward fully pricing the meeting. The restrained tone on sovereign spreads should dampen volatility, which GS thinks skews toward 5y outperformance on the EUR curve.

GS expects energy to remain the main driver of front-end rates in Europe, supporting a flatter 2s5s curve. TTF prices are near GS commodity strategists' upside scenario and rates vol is elevated versus GS's fair value model.

GS sees EU bonds as roughly fair against the broader EGB complex, trading in line with euro area aggregate fundamentals. Over 2027 GS sees risks skewed toward EU outperformance versus peers because NGEU issuance ends in 2026 and EU issuance roughly halves to €70bn.

GS economists expect the BoE MPC to deliver its first hike of the cycle next week, with one further hike in February. With substantial tightening priced, GS sees a high hurdle for further front-end cheapening. Renewed energy pressure is the main upside risk, and in an adverse energy scenario the UK front end would underperform Europe.

The GBP-EUR front-end vol differential has compressed well below what the rates differential implies. GS says relative value is tilted long GBP versus EUR front-end vol, expressed by owning front-end GBP receivers versus EUR, most likely to work on energy de-escalation.

The UK Autumn Budget broadly matched expectations. The deficit path was revised £13bn higher per year on average and headroom fell to £15bn, mostly from higher interest costs. The gilt remit rose only £4bn and the long-term share fell from about 10% to 6%, which supports Gilts versus swaps.

GS sees limited scope for broader UK risk premia to compress, since fiscal pressures are pushed out rather than resolved. Gross gilt supply is expected to exceed £300bn in 2027/28. GS expects the 10y point to underperform on the UK curve versus peers and prefers expressing the supply improvement through asset swaps rather than outright duration.

GS economists moved their expected BoJ hike to December. Reasons are Ueda's emphasis on upside price risks, caution about yen weakness if the Fed hikes, and receding fiscal concerns. GS expects further AI concerns to support JGB richening, long-end outperformance and bull flattening.

The RBNZ held the OCR in a surprise 4-3 vote despite guiding toward further increases. GS economists now expect two hikes, in December and March, below market pricing in pace and magnitude. GS favors NZD 2s10s steepeners because NZD term premium is the lowest among peers.

GS expects the RBA to hike next week as the final hike of the cycle. GS keeps a preference for AUD front-end flattening such as 2s5s, but closes its IRZ6U7 flattener for a potential profit of 25bp because the asymmetry around the RBA meeting is less clear.

trade_ideas.description: Long 5s on the 2s5s30s UST fly (receive 5y). Entry -44bp, target -60bp, stop -35bp
trade_ideas.rationale: Front-end hike risk is reduced, 5s tend to outperform during and after hikes, and the long end faces refunding risk.

trade_ideas.description: CAD 1y1y vs 1y or CORH7Z7 flatteners. Entry 40bp, target 25bp, stop 50bp
trade_ideas.rationale: The cumulative hike premium in the CAD front end looks excessive given inflation below 2%, AI volatility weighing on peers' hike pricing, and likely pull-forward rather than a larger cumulative amount.
trade_ideas.risk: Stop at 50bp. A December hike is possible if inflation surprises up or a trade deal is reached.

trade_ideas.rationale: A more patient RBNZ should lower near-term hike expectations, while elevated uncertainty and inflation above target support term premium further out. NZD term premium is the lowest among peers, and carry is favorable.

trade_ideas.description: Own front-end GBP receivers versus EUR (long GBP vs EUR front-end vol)
trade_ideas.rationale: The GBP-EUR front-end vol differential is compressed well below what the rates differential implies.
trade_ideas.risk: The dislocation may persist. It most likely normalizes on energy de-escalation.

trade_ideas.description: Gilts versus swaps via asset swaps, preferred over outright duration
trade_ideas.rationale: Reduced QT and lower long-end issuance support Gilts. Long-end swap spreads have widened about 3bp since the September QT announcement, with scope for modest further widening.
trade_ideas.risk: Longer-term UK fiscal challenges are unresolved.

trade_ideas.description: AUD front-end flattening such as 2s5s. The IRZ6U7 flattener is closed for a potential profit of 25bp
trade_ideas.rationale: AUD flattening can extend in either a bullish spillover or a renewed hawkish scenario.
trade_ideas.risk: Less clear asymmetry around next week's RBA meeting.

trade_ideas.description: Closed: receive 10s on the 5s10s30s SOFR fly, opened 9-Oct-26, closed 30-Oct-26 for +3bp
trade_ideas.rationale: GS rotates to 5s because the value on the curve is now somewhat better there.

risk_factors: Further AI-related risk asset volatility could push yields lower, or a weaker risk tone could magnify the reaction to a downside surprise in next Friday's US labor report.
A cut in long-end Treasury auction sizes at the refunding is a risk. Unchanged sizes could instead disappoint the market's lean toward reduced sizes and cause long-end underperformance.
Energy escalation is a clear risk to BoE front-end pricing, and an adverse energy scenario would hit the UK front end harder than Europe.
A stronger inflation surprise could bring a third Fed hike in March, and a December BoC hike is possible if inflation surprises up or a trade deal is reached.
Fiscal news could weigh on long-end JGBs again, and unresolved UK fiscal challenges and gilt supply above £300bn in 2027/28 limit risk premia compression.
French rating downgrade speculation and sovereign spread pressures could affect EU bonds and ECB hike pricing.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots the 1m correlation of the 10y UST yield with Brent and with AI-related equities from Oct-25 to Oct-26. GS says AI-related volatility has taken over from energy as the driver of directional yield moves.
Exhibit 2 plots money fund AUM growth. GS says it has stalled since summer.
Exhibit 4 compares EUR 3m5y implied vol with the EUR 2s5s30s fly. GS says 5s ought to outperform in a more restrained vol environment.
Exhibit 6 plots the GBP-EUR 1y1y implied vol differential against a fit on the 1y1y OIS differential. GS says the vol differential has diverged from the rate differential.
Exhibit 7 plots the change in projected gross gilt issuance, October versus March 2026 OBR forecast. GS says issuance was revised higher for 2027/28 and 2028/29.
vol_and_positioning: GS estimates real money is still underweight duration, though it sees runway for the rally to extend if risk asset volatility persists.
Fund managers' duration risk appetite has stayed cautious even though longer-term bond funds have seen healthy inflows.
Euro rates volatility is elevated versus GS's fair value model. GS links 5s performance on the EUR curve to the level of rate vol.
The GBP-EUR front-end vol differential has compressed well below what the rates differential implies, so GS favors long GBP versus EUR front-end vol.
Positioning monitor readings: US option implied position indicator score 0, GS fund positioning indicator -3, US data response indicator -1.

CFTC duration-weighted spec net positions are negative across all UST and SOFR contracts (SFR -74.5, TU -28.9, FV -44.4, TY -56.8, TN -12.6, US -12.4, WN -58.3 $mm/bp). Asset managers are net long in TU, FV, TY, TN, US and WN.
geopolitical: The Iran conflict is cited as a driver of rates after next week's US midterm elections, together with perceived implications for AI.
Energy escalation is flagged as a clear risk to BoE front-end pricing, and TTF prices are close to GS commodities strategists' upside scenario.
French sovereign rating downgrade speculation has raised investor focus on EU bonds and increased beta to OAT and BTPs.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects Treasury to keep 10-to-30y coupon auction sizes unchanged. Long-end spreads are wide to fair value, so a large reduction is unnecessary.
tension_points.bear_case: Market expectations lean toward reduced long-end sizes. Unchanged sizes could disappoint and cause long-end underperformance on the spread curve. A cut is a risk to GS's base case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reduction in long-end auction sizes at next week's refunding announcement.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price 13bp of hikes by year-end and about 100bp through end-2027 after the BoC's hawkish tone.
tension_points.bear_case: GS sees the premium as excessive. Trim and median inflation are below 2%, AI volatility weighs on peers' hike pricing, and upside data would pull hikes forward rather than add to the total.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation data that meaningfully surprises to the upside, or a trade deal, would raise the risk of a December BoC hike.

tension_points.theme: UK gilt supply vs fiscal risk
tension_points.bull_case: The remit rose only £4bn and the long-term share fell from about 10% to 6%, which supports Gilts versus swaps.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal challenges are unresolved, gross gilt supply is expected to exceed £300bn in 2027/28, and the headroom is smaller, which leaves the 10y point likely to underperform.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed energy pressure or fiscal slippage would undercut the front-end and risk-premia views.

tension_points.theme: Fed hike pace and strategy meetings
tension_points.bull_case: The curve steepened on Warsh's strategy-meeting announcement, which was read as dovish.
tension_points.bear_case: GS would be surprised if the schedule change constrained the Fed from acting, and GS economists still see a December hike with a risk of a third hike in March.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An upside inflation surprise that brings the third hike in March into play.
